event.name: SecureCrypt CTF
event.tagline: Break the encryption company that rolled its own crypto.

challenges.title: Hidden in Plain Sight
challenges.description: SecureCrypt's site leaves clues lying around. Every website has a file that tells search engines what to ignore. Find it, then follow what it points to.
hints: It mentions a .bak file you can open directly.

challenges.title: Open Sesame
challenges.description: The staff login talks to a database with a carelessly built query. Make it let you in without a real password.
hints: What does a single quote ' do to a SQL string?
Look up: SQL injection login bypass.

challenges.title: Spilling Secrets
challenges.description: The engine search box is just as careless as the login. Make it return data it shouldn't — the staff password list and the hidden records.
hints: First work out how many columns the query selects.

challenges.title: Have a Cookie
challenges.description: After you log in, inspect your session cookie. It may not be as secret as it looks. Become an administrator.
hints: Decode the cookie — it's just Base64.
Change the role and re-encode it.

challenges.title: Pop!
challenges.description: The search box trusts your input too much. Get a JavaScript alert box to appear on the page, then show your instructor.
hints: Try a <script> tag in the search term.

challenges.title: Bronze Engine
challenges.description:
You downloaded the Bronze encryption engine via the IDOR. Open it in Ghidra, find the single secret key, and decrypt this in CyberChef.

Ciphertext (hex):
040e0305393a72301d73311d2c2d361d272c21303b32362b2d2c3f
hints: The binary isn't stripped — read the encrypt function.
CyberChef: From Hex → XOR with the one-byte key.

challenges.title: Silver Engine
challenges.description:
The Silver engine uses a whole password as the key, repeated across the message. Find the password in the program.

Ciphertext (hex):
367832340c4241141555074219572d0f434d2c0003011e082f4316121c4d
hints: CyberChef: From Hex → XOR with the password (UTF8).

challenges.title: Gold Engine
challenges.description:
The flagship engine does three things to your message, one after another. Read the code to get the ORDER right, then undo each step in reverse.

Ciphertext (base64):
Dok6MFUPgFZsI2MXJV8mHXkqQA4NFXkZQmwUDmog
hints: Encryption order is XOR → add a fixed offset → Base64.
Decrypt in reverse: From Base64 → SUB the offset → XOR the key.
